taxonomic_note: World Flora Online accepts the nominate subspecies and includes Texas in its native range. Species-level and other-infraspecific records are not transferred automatically.
look_here_first: Start with a moist-site rhizomatous white-panicle aster. Count 1–3(–5) leafy bracts along a typical peduncle; test relatively PLIABLE/non-waxy lanceolate leaves against stiff waxy S. praealtum, where underside veins form regular isodiametric areoles and 5–12+ peduncle bracts. For the nominate infraspecific assignment, inspect SHORTER outer phyllaries (usually 1/3–2/3 the inner), and NO large leafy bracts directly subtending heads; compare var. hesperium, whose outer phyllaries can be 2/3+ inner with conspicuous foliaceous bracts. This is not proof of three target-zone counties.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays and Travis are locked under the nominate concept. Williamson evidence in the review is var. hesperium and is not counted toward subsp. lanceolatum.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is independent from native-range certification.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use growth form, leaf shape, panicle architecture, and infraspecific characters together; species-level white aster appearance is not enough for subspecies assignment.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. praealtum: more waxy/stiff progressively reduced leaves, regular polygonal underside areoles, 5–12+ peduncle bracts. S. lanceolatum: fewer 1–3(–5) bracts, upper surface generally not waxy and underside vein areoles irregular/not prominent. For nominate concept, outer phyllaries normally only 1/3–2/3 as long as inner, not large foliaceous subtending heads; contrast S. lanceolatum var./subsp. hesperium with 2/3+ ratio. Existing subsp. lanceolatum range hold remains.
